evidence.excerpt: This book chapter provides a self-contained introduction to cost-sensitive classification intended for laboratory informaticians and biostatisticians with limited background in machine learning. It covers the formulation of asymmetric loss functions, the construction of cost matrices from clinical outcome data, threshold-moving as a post-hoc strategy, and direct cost-minimising training through modified learning objectives. Each concept is illustrated with worked examples drawn from haematology, microbiology, and clinical chemistry laboratory settings. The chapter also discusses common pitfalls, including the use of accuracy as a performance metric when classes are imbalanced, the conflation of probabilistic calibration with discrimination, and the failure to propagate cost assumptions into cross-validation. Pseudocode is provided for the main algorithms. The target audience is practitioners who need to communicate method choices to clinical colleagues and regulatory reviewers.
